data.body:
Split pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1496

**The seams this ticket originally proposed are both unsafe.** Worth recording, because the reason is invisible from the file itself.

Two unit tests load this conftest by path and drive it with `monkeypatch.setattr(harness, "_request", fake)`. That rebinds a name in *conftest's* globals, so it only reaches callers whose own module globals are that namespace. Move `_request` — or any of its patched-through callers (`_create_scratch_project`, `_assert_project_capabilities`, `_leaked_harness_tokens`, `_sweep_leaked_harness_tokens`, `wait_for_jira_dc_ready`, `jira_dc_project`) — to a sibling module and the moved function resolves the REAL `_request`. The unit tier then starts issuing live HTTP. That fails OPEN: nothing errors, the stub just silently stops applying. Both clusters the ticket named (PAT sweep, scratch-project provisioning) are entirely inside that set.

**What was extracted instead:** the J11 store-copy / DC-client cluster — `dc_transport`, `dc_store_copy_repo`, `bound_dc_issue`. It already carried its own banner comment in the file explaining it sits in conftest only because two sibling suites need it; `bound_dc_issue` consumes the other two and all three draw on `_dc_support`, so it is a real call-graph cluster, not a slice. No unit test references any member. 203 lines moved to `_dc_fixtures.py` (248 with its header, clear of the 100-line floor); conftest is 758.

Mechanics: conftest re-imports the three names so pytest still collects them as its own attributes (verified with `pytest --fixtures`), the sibling directory goes on `sys.path` the same way `_TESTS_DIR`/`engine_dir()`/`_SCRIPTS_DIR` already do, and the base URL reaches the moved fixtures via a new session-scoped `jira_dc_base_url` fixture rather than a second copy of `_BASE`.

**Coverage added** (3 cells in `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py`): the fixture surface survives the by-path load; every monkeypatched name is still *defined* in conftest, not merely re-exported into it; and the file stays within the cap read from `.github/module-size-limit.txt` rather than a restated number. The middle cell is the one that earns its keep — it is the only thing standing between a future split and a silent un-stubbing that would surface 35 minutes into a live harness run.

**One pre-existing guard needed widening.** `tests/unit/test_live_dc_isolation_controls_59b2.py` greps the fixture source for `for cloud_var in CLOUD_CREDENTIAL_VARS:` to prove the credential list is not duplicated — and read `conftest.py` by name. Since `dc_store_copy_repo` holds that loop, the guard would have reported it DELETED when it had only moved. It now scans the harness's whole fixture surface, asserting the same invariant without being keyed to a filename. It caught the move correctly, which is a point in its favour.
